title: Around the World in Eighty Days: A Race Across America
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Fogg, Aouda, and Passepartout arrive in San Francisco and board a train east across the United States. Detective Fix continues to follow them. He still suspects Fogg of stealing from the bank, but he needs the party to reach England before an arrest can happen. The train crosses wide plains and difficult tracks. Fogg watches the schedule while the others look for the next delay that might cost him the wager. The train crosses bridges and open country while Fogg checks the timetable. Aouda and Passepartout watch the landscape change from their carriage. Fix stays close to the group; although he still suspects Fogg, he now wants him to reach England, where an arrest can be made. The journey cannot wait for every obstacle to clear. At each stop they look for the next departure and listen for news about the line ahead.

During the crossing, attackers board the train. Passepartout is carried away in the confusion. The train moves on, but Fogg refuses to leave his servant behind. He takes a small group of men back across the plain to search. They find Passepartout alive and bring him to Aouda. The rescue has cost time, and the original train is gone. Fogg must find another way to make the next connection. Aouda sees how much he values the people travelling with him, even though he rarely speaks about his feelings.

The party hires a wind-powered sled to cross snowy ground and catch up with the route. It moves quickly, but the weather and the distance make the ride uncertain. They reach the coast and prepare for the Atlantic crossing. Passepartout is safe, and the group remains together after the attack. Fogg has given up hours to save him. The wager is still possible, but every lost connection leaves less time to reach the Reform Club in London.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days: The Last Day
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Fogg and his companions need a ship across the Atlantic to finish their journey. No captain will take them on exactly the route they need, so Fogg pays for a vessel and changes its course. Fuel runs low; the crew burns wooden parts of the ship to keep it moving. They reach the British coast and take a train toward London. Fogg believes he has only a small amount of time left before the eighty-day deadline. At the harbour Fogg learns that the usual steamer has already gone. He searches for another captain willing to sail and boards the Henrietta. Its captain has a different destination, so Fogg offers the crew money to change course. Passepartout watches the argument and hopes that the strange bargain will still bring them home in time. There is no other ship ready to help them.

title: The Secret Garden: Mary Comes to Misselthwaite
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Mary Lennox grows up in India while servants do nearly everything for her. A sickness kills her parents and many people in their household. She is sent to England to live with her uncle at Misselthwaite Manor. Mrs. Medlock brings her through its long corridors and tells her that her uncle stays away and that many rooms are closed. Mary is used to being obeyed, but the people in this house have work of their own. She spends lonely days inside until a servant called Martha speaks to her about the moor outside.

Martha talks plainly to Mary and tells her about her family. Mary starts to walk in the fresh air. She meets Ben Weatherstaff, a gardener who does not hurry to please her, and notices a robin near a walled garden. She hears that the garden has been locked since her aunt died. No one will show her its door. Mary returns to the wall and watches where the bird lands, looking for a way to learn more about the hidden place. Martha tells Mary about a skipping rope and shows her how to use it. Mary is clumsy at first and has to stop for breath, but she tries again outside. The exercise keeps her in the garden longer. Ben Weatherstaff continues his work nearby, and the robin hops close enough for her to watch without speaking.

One day the robin hops beside a patch of earth. Mary sees something buried there and digs out a small key. She remembers Martha's story about the locked garden. She has not found its door yet, so she keeps the key and searches along the wall. The quiet house still holds many closed rooms, but outside Mary now has a question to follow. She goes back to look for the robin and the place it seems to know.

She meets Ben Weatherstaff, a gardener who does not hurry to please her, and notices a robin near a walled garden. She hears that the garden has been locked since her aunt died. Ben Weatherstaff continues his work nearby, and the robin hops close enough for her to watch without speaking. Ben Weatherstaff works while Mary asks questions. He says little about the garden, yet the robin moves near the same wall each day. Mary begins to return without anyone telling her to.

One day the robin hops beside a patch of earth. Mary sees something buried there and digs out a small key. She remembers Martha's story about the locked garden. She cannot ask her uncle where the door is because he is away, so she must keep searching herself.

title: The Secret Garden: A Garden and a Hidden Voice
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Mary follows the robin along the garden wall and finds a hidden door. The key she dug from the earth turns in its lock. Inside, branches cover the paths and dead stems tangle around the beds. Mary looks closely and sees green shoots growing beneath the dry plants. She begins to clear a small space and returns whenever she can. She keeps the discovery secret because she does not want the door closed again.

Martha's brother Dickon knows plants and animals. Mary trusts him with the secret and shows him the garden. He brings tools and seeds, and together they decide what can grow. title: The Secret Garden: Colin Joins the Garden
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Mary tells Colin about the hidden garden and asks whether he wants to see it. He has spent so long inside that the idea frightens him, yet he wants to know why Mary and Dickon return there every day. They arrange for him to be taken out in his chair without drawing attention from adults who might stop the visit. He sees the paths, birds, and green shoots for himself. The place is different from the sickroom where he has spent most of his time.

Dickon points out young plants and the work the children have done. Colin begins by watching from his chair. Soon he asks for a closer look and wants a task of his own. Mary and Dickon help him take part. They return together, and Colin starts to move more. He tries standing with support and is surprised by what he can do. He asks his friends to keep his progress private until he is ready to tell his father. Colin first sees the garden from his chair. Dickon shows him birds and new leaves while Mary points out the beds they have cleared. On later visits Colin asks to come closer to the plants. He wants to touch them and help, even when a small task takes time. Mary and Dickon make room for him beside them.

Mary has changed since she arrived at the manor too. She no longer waits alone for servants to entertain her. Each morning she goes outside to meet Dickon and Colin. The three look for new shoots, work in the soil, and talk about their next visit. Colin still has difficult days, but he now has people beside him and a place he wants to reach again. He begins to imagine meeting his father outdoors rather than from his bed.
shortSummary: Mary brings Colin a secret instead of treating him like a patient. He becomes curious about the garden and asks to see it.

title: The Secret Garden: A Changed House
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Colin returns to the hidden garden with Mary and Dickon whenever he can. At first he needed his chair to reach the beds. Now he practises standing and walking among the plants. The children keep his progress quiet because he wants his father to see it for himself. They work in the soil and watch the garden grow while Colin tries to go a little farther each day. Mary and Dickon are beside him when he needs to rest. He talks about meeting his father outside instead of being visited in his sickroom. The garden is no longer covered in dead branches. Mary and Dickon have cleared paths, planted seeds, and watched new leaves appear. Colin knows that his father remembers the place from before it was locked. He wants their first meeting to happen among the living plants. Every day he asks his friends for another chance to practise walking down the path.

Archibald Craven has stayed away from Misselthwaite Manor since his wife died. He travels with memories of the garden she loved but cannot bring himself to visit it. A dream about her and a letter from his brother draw him home. He walks through the grounds toward the long-closed garden. From beyond the wall he hears children's voices. He stops, surprised that anyone has entered a place locked for years, then follows the sound toward the hidden door.

Inside, Colin has been practising with his friends. He is standing when his father arrives. Archibald can hardly believe that the boy before him is his son. Colin moves toward him, and they embrace among the plants. Mary and Dickon watch their meeting. Father and son leave the garden together and walk back toward the house. The servants see them coming side by side. Mary, who once waited alone in the silent manor, has helped open both the garden and the family's life again.
shortSummary: Colin continues visiting the garden and grows stronger with regular movement and encouragement. The children decide to keep his improvement private until he can surprise his father.

A dream about her and a letter from his brother draw him home. He walks through the grounds toward the long-closed garden; from beyond the wall he hears children's voices. He stops, surprised that anyone has entered a place locked for years, then follows the sound toward the hidden door. Craven expects the same closed house he left. He does not know Mary found the key or that the children have cared for the garden. Their voices make him hurry to the door.

Colin moves toward him, and they embrace among the plants; Mary and Dickon watch their meeting. Father and son leave the garden together and walk back toward the house. The servants see them coming side by side. Mary, who once waited alone in the silent manor, has helped open both the garden and the family's life again. For years the garden had held painful memories for him. Now he finds his son there with friends. Colin walks beside him on the way back, and the household sees the change without needing a long explanation.
